RequestRecord.description: An upsert of an existing agent: the configure request bringing it to this configuration between its turns

Outcome.description: result.code names a run's failure where it has a name: cancelled (a stop cancelled it before it began), aborted (stopped while it ran), model_stream_stalled (its model stopped answering, past every retry), turn_limit, context_too_large (its stored Pi context range exceeds the runtime byte limit), spend_limit, agent_loop_limit (a sub-agent's notification landed without a turn: its chain reached its wake cap), output_missing, model_key_missing, model_key_invalid. result.stopped is input_required when the turn waits on human input, listed in result.inputs. A run's result also has reply, replyIndex, files, toolErrors and toolCalls: every tool call it made (the first 100), as {tool, toolCallId?, innerCallId?, ok, code?, agentId?} (agentId: the child a delegate or spawn_agent call ran), without arguments or results. result.output is a structured answer, for a prompt sent with output. result.usage.subagentCostUsd is what its children spent, result.usage.imageCostUsd what its generate_image calls spent, and result.usage.decisionCostUsd what its decide calls spent. result.servedModel is the model that made its last response (provider/model-id); result.modelError, when a model call failed it, says how: {errorClass, providerStatus?, retryable, model} (ModelFailure)

workspaceId.description: Workspace for spend attribution. New agents inherit their definition workspace when omitted. null leaves them unassigned. Later moves keep earlier usage in its original workspace.

mcp.description: The application's attached MCP server: its tools/list, whose tools the agent calls back through the application's connection. The SDKs send it

definition.description: Make the agent from this definition (GET /v1/definitions). It supplies the model, system prompt, thinking level, fileTools and tool sources; name, type, ttlSeconds, mounts and initialMessages given here override its defaults. model, thinkingLevel, maxOutputTokens, temperature, language, fileTools, codeMode and runLimits given here are the agent's own: applying the definition later keeps them. systemPrompt cannot be given with a definition; use systemPromptAppend

model.description: A model id from GET /v1/models; the runtime default when omitted

systemPromptAppend.description: Text after the system prompt, e.g. per-conversation context. The agent's own: applying its definition replaces the prompt and keeps this

language.description: Its primary language (Language). On an upsert of an existing agent, null removes it and leaving it out keeps the one it has

initialMessages.description: History to begin with (a conversation from elsewhere): Pi user, assistant and toolResult messages, and compactionSummary messages, the last of which stands in for everything before it. Only when the agent is made; at most 16 MB of JSON. See the multi-user guide

format.description: anthropic: Messages API messages; openai-responses: Responses API input items; openai-chat: Chat Completions messages

model.description: The model that wrote the assistant turns, as provider/model-id: its signed thinking or encrypted reasoning is sent back to that same model; any other model gets reasoning as text, or none

importMessages.description: History to begin with in another API's format, with its tool calls and results, converted to Pi messages (initialMessages; not both). Images must be base64 or data: URLs; system and developer messages are left out (the agent's prompt replaces them). Only when the agent is made

fileTools.description: false: the model gets no file tools (read, write, edit, ls, glob, grep), only present_file; the mounts stay open to fs in js_exec, attachments and tool outputs. For applications with file tools of their own

codeMode.description: false: no js_exec (code mode). The model calls every tool directly, and the system prompt carries only the runtime text those tools need: for an agent with no tools (with fileTools: false too, and no builtins or tool sources), only the application's instructions and a short note on who sent each message. For a tool-less agent, such as a classifier. Best set when the agent is made: changed later, its tools change, while a conversation under way keeps the runtime text it began with

ttlSeconds.description: Agent lifetime: 60 to 31622400 seconds, or null to live until deleted. Default: until deleted for an agent made with an Idempotency-Key, 86400 for one made without

idleTtlSeconds.description: Instead of ttlSeconds: the agent lives this long (60 to 31622400 seconds) from its latest run, so one in use is kept and one left idle expires. Not with ttlSeconds

mounts.description: Volumes for the agent's file tools. Its own workspace volume is at /workspace beside them unless they include {workspace: false} or a mount at /workspace; {workspace: true, path?} places it. The first is where relative paths resolve

remount.description: An upsert of an existing agent: true sets the mounts given, between its turns, where other mounts are a 409

subject.description: Who the agent acts for (a user id in your app): the `sub` of the identity tokens its tool servers with auth "runtime" get. Set only here

context.description: Claims your tool servers need (org, workspace, thread…), carried as `ctx` in its identity tokens; at most 4 KB. Set only here

builtins.description: Tools the runtime answers itself (web_fetch, web_search, x_search, schedule, ask_user, delegate, generate_image, agents, decide), for an agent without a definition; one made from a definition has its definition's. An upsert without builtins leaves the agent none

decide.description: The decide tool (typed questions answered with probabilities by a decision model; see Decisions) is every agent's by default, except one with no js_exec and no other tools. false: none; true: even then. Not for an agent made from a definition: its definition's decide applies

mcpServers.description: Remote MCP servers whose tools the runtime calls for the agent, for an agent without a definition; one made from a definition has its definition's. No credentials: auth "runtime" or none. An upsert without mcpServers leaves the agent none

keyScope.description: A key scope (PUT /v1/key-scopes/{scope}/providers/{provider}) whose keys the agent's model calls use first, before the tenant's own

bucket.description: With end-user credits on (/v1/end-user-settings): the bucket of its subject's credit its runs spend from (its daily allowance first, then their balance). Default "default"

MaxOutputTokens.description: The most the model writes in one response, at most its own maximum (maxTokens in GET /v1/models); default that maximum. A response that reaches it ends with stopReason "length". A Claude model on a thinking budget gets the budget on top; elsewhere reasoning counts toward it. Compaction summaries keep the runtime's own

Temperature.description: Sampling temperature, 0 to 2; default the provider's. Lower is more deterministic. 400 for a model that takes none: Claude Opus 4.7 and later, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable models, models that always reason (o-series, GPT-5), and any reasoning model at a thinkingLevel other than off. Compaction summaries keep the runtime's own

DataCollection.description: "deny": the agent's OpenRouter model calls (turns and compaction summaries) go only to hosts that do not collect their data: OpenRouter's provider.data_collection, which skips providers whose data policy says they may train on it. A filter, so OpenRouter still balances load among the rest. Default: none (OpenRouter's default). Other providers ignore it

path.description: Where the agent's file tools see the volume, e.g. /workspace

subpath.description: Mount only this directory of the volume

notify.description: Prompt the agent when others change files under this mount

path.description: With true: where it is mounted, absolute and normalized (default /workspace), e.g. /scratch beside a project volume at /workspace

WorkspaceMount.description: The agent's own workspace volume, where attachments, tool outputs and scratch files go. It is mounted at /workspace beside the mounts given (last) unless they leave it out: true places it at this position (at `path`), false leaves it out, and a mount given at /workspace takes its place

Builtin.description: agents: sub-agents in the background (spawn_agent, wait_agent, list_agents), with the delegate settings; workflow: run_workflow, a script that coordinates sub-agents, with the workflow settings

agents.description: Who the model may delegate to: definitions (a new child agent for each call) and existing agents by key

instructions.description: Let the model start a child with instructions of its own instead, on its own model

maxDepth.description: How deep delegation may go: a child is depth 1, its child depth 2. Default 2

maxParallel.description: delegate calls of one run in flight at once (more wait their turn), and the agent's background sub-agents running at once (spawn_agent past it is refused). Default 4

DelegateSettings.description: With the delegate or agents builtin: who the agent may hand tasks to. Not with a definition, whose own it takes

anyOf.description: A definition's key or id; the model sees it by that name

name.description: What the model calls it; default: the definition's or agent's key

agent.description: An existing agent's key. The agent keeps its history across calls; a definition makes a new child each call

description.description: What it is for, for the model; default: the definition's description

agents.description: Who a workflow script may coordinate: definitions (a new child agent for each agent() call) and existing agents by key

instructions.description: Let the script start a child with instructions of its own instead, on its own model

maxAgents.description: The most agent() calls one workflow run may make. Default 32

maxDepth.description: How deep a chain of agents may go: a child is depth 1, its child depth 2. Default 2

maxParallel.description: Agent calls of one workflow in flight at once; more queue inside the script. Default 4

WorkflowSettings.description: With the workflow builtin: who the agent's workflow scripts may coordinate. Not with a definition, whose own it takes

name.description: Its tools reach the model as <name>__<tool>: 1–32 letters and digits, single underscores between them

url.description: The server's Streamable HTTP (or older SSE) endpoint; https, on a public address

denyTools.description: None of these of its tools

exposure.description: How the model calls its tools: directly, from js_exec (the default), or both

timeoutMs.description: How long a call may go without an answer; default 60000. Each progress notification the server sends restarts it, up to 1200000 in all

audience.description: With auth "runtime": the tokens' aud, when not the server's url (behind a proxy, say): a URL on its origin, or a name that stays when the server moves, urn:camelrun:<tenant>:<name>

default.description: never (the default), always, or destructive: tools annotated destructiveHint (MCP), operations other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS (OpenAPI)

tools.description: Per tool, by its own name: overrides the default

approval.description: Which tools the user approves before each call. Those tools are declared to the model directly; an approved call carries _meta["agent-runtime/approval"] and an approval claim in its identity token

fileArguments.description: Whether the model may send the agent's files to its tools ({"$file": path}), and the runtime saves files they link to. Default on with auth "runtime", off otherwise: another party's server could be sent any file the agent can read

auth.description: Each request carries a JWT the runtime signs, naming the tenant, agent, subject, context and actor (no definition); verify it against /.well-known/jwks.json. The only auth an agent's own server takes

InlineMcpServerInput.description: An MCP server of the agent's (or run's) own, as a definition's is, but with no credentials: no headers and no bearer token (a 400 says to use a definition, which seals them once). Not listed when saved: a server that cannot be listed shows in a run's sourceErrors

SpendLimitInput.description: The most the agent may spend on model calls (their token cost, compaction included) from when this is set: a new value starts counting from zero. At it, new prompts get 402 and a running turn ends with stopped "spend_limit"

maxResponses.description: Model responses one run may make, compaction summaries included; default and at most the runtime's maximum (1,000 unless its operator set another)

maxSeconds.description: Seconds one run may take from when it began; default and at most the runtime's maximum (7,200, 2 hours, unless its operator set another). A turn still inside a model request or tool call 60 seconds past it is aborted then, with stopped "turn_limit"

firstTokenSeconds.description: Seconds one model request may wait for the model's first token (text, thinking or a tool call) before it fails as stalled and is retried; default the runtime's (120, or 300 for a reasoning model at thinkingLevel high and up)

idleSeconds.description: Seconds a model response may go quiet once it streams before it fails as stalled and is retried; default the runtime's (45)

contextTokens.description: The most context one model request carries, in tokens: older context is summarized (compacted) before a request would pass it, starting in the background somewhat below it. Default the model's context window, and never above it. At least 20,000. A long-lived agent on a large-window model costs less per request with a lower one, since each request reads its whole context

RunLimits.description: The most one run may take (model responses, seconds); an agent from a definition gets the definition's unless this is given

ModelHeaders.description: Non-secret headers sent on each of the agent's model calls, after a key scope entry's, e.g. cf-aig-metadata. At most 20 and 8 KB; never authorization, x-api-key, x-goog-api-key, cf-aig-authorization, chatgpt-account-id, x-agent-runtime-identity, x-amz-* or transport headers

text.description: The message. It may be left out when the message attaches audio, whose transcript is then the message

actor.description: Who is acting in this turn (a user id in your app): `act` in its tools' identity tokens

id.description: The sender's id in your app; the model may rely on it

name.description: Display name, chosen by the sender

from.description: Who sent this message. The model sees it in a block only the runtime can write; `from.id` is also the turn's actor unless `actor` is given

requestId.description: Idempotency: retrying with the same id returns the same request. The user message records it, so a UI can match its own bubble

allowDisconnected.description: Run even though the agent's tools need its application and none is connected (else 409 APPLICATION_NOT_CONNECTED): its calls then fail as not connected

whileRunning.description: What happens if the agent is working on a turn when this arrives. queue (default): it runs as the next turn. steer: the running turn takes it after its current step. The 202 says so at once (steer: "accepted"; "queued" when no turn could take it), and this request completes as soon as the turn takes the message (steeredInto names the turn, whose own request has its outcome; a steer_taken event marks it), so steered messages never wait for the turn's end, nor count against the agent's queue once taken. If the turn ends first, it runs as a turn of its own. With no turn running, both start one

allOf.description: This run's own budget in USD: it ends before its next model request once it has spent this. The agent's spendLimit is unchanged and counts the run too

bucket.description: With end-user credits on (/v1/end-user-settings): the bucket of the agent's subject this run spends from, instead of the agent's. Only the tenant may set it

runLimits.description: This run's own limits: at most this many model responses, or seconds. They only lower the agent's runLimits and the runtime's; at one, the run ends with stopped "turn_limit"

schema.description: A JSON Schema for an object (type: "object"; at most 64 KB)

output.description: Structured output: the agent ends this run by calling a final_output tool whose arguments are the schema, checked against it (a call that does not fit goes back to the model with what is wrong). The run's outcome.result.output is that object. A model that answers in text instead is asked once more, with a reminder; a run that still ends without an output fails with code output_missing. The tool stays declared until a prompt without output. Not with whileRunning: steer

history.description: Deprecated and ignored: every run sees the agent's history (Pi's compaction keeps its context bounded). Accepted so existing callers do not fail. For a run that sees no history, use POST /v1/runs

metadata.description: Your own key-value data about this message (its source, a client-side id): at most 16 keys of 1–64 characters, values of at most 512. Kept on the user message (history, events, snapshots) and the request, and sent with its run's webhook events; never shown to the model

path.description: A file in the agent's mounts, e.g. one uploaded with PUT /v1/agents/{id}/uploads/{requestId}/{name}

transcribe.description: Whether this file is transcribed for the model (audio only): default true for audio (an audio/* content type), false for anything else. See the voice and audio guide

data.description: The file's bytes, base64: at most 4 MiB across a message's inline files

transcribe.description: Whether this file is transcribed for the model (audio only): default true for audio (an audio/* content type), false for anything else. See the voice and audio guide

url.description: An https URL the runtime fetches the file from (public addresses only; at most 64 MiB)

transcribe.description: Whether this file is transcribed for the model (audio only): default true for audio (an audio/* content type), false for anything else. See the voice and audio guide

files.description: Attached files (at most 20): saved in the agent's workspace under uploads/<requestId>/, named in the message, and shown natively (images, PDFs) to models that take them. Audio is transcribed before the request is accepted, and the model reads the transcript

PromptInput.description: A first prompt, as POST /v1/agents/{id}/prompt takes it, sent once the agent is made: it runs as soon as the agent has started, so a new conversation needs one call. Give it a requestId: a retry of the create (same Idempotency-Key) with the same requestId makes no second agent and sends no second prompt

definition.description: The definition the agent was made from, and the revision it has

tools.description: The tools your application declared, which it answers

toolSources.description: Every source of the agent's tools, in order of precedence, and what each offers the model

fileTools.description: Present when the model gets no file tools but present_file

codeMode.description: Present when the agent has no js_exec, and the model calls every tool directly

keyScope.description: The key scope its model calls take keys from first

bucket.description: The bucket of its subject's credit its runs spend from (end-user credits); null: "default"

builtins.description: The tools the runtime answers itself: its own, or its definition's

decide.description: Its decide setting, its own or its definition's: false (none), true (asked for), or null (the default: the tool unless it has no js_exec and no other tools). The tool is offered only where the account has an OpenRouter key decisions can use; toolSources shows it

allOf.description: Who it may delegate to, with the delegate or agents builtin
Who its workflow scripts may coordinate, with the workflow builtin

mcpServers.description: Its remote MCP servers: its own, or its definition's (without credentials' values)

parentRunId.description: For a child a delegate or spawn_agent call made: the run of parentAgentId that made it

spent.description: Model spend since the limit was set

allOf.description: Its own run limits, as set; null: the runtime's
The most its model writes in one response, as set; null: the model's maximum
Its model's sampling temperature, as set; null: the provider's default
Its OpenRouter calls' data policy, as set; null: OpenRouter's default

queuedRuns.description: Runs accepted and waiting behind it (prompts, steered messages not yet read, continues, executions, resumes)

connected.description: application: whether your application is connected to answer its tools

exposure.description: The source's configured exposure; each tool shows the one it has

headerNames.description: Headers the server gets; their values are never returned

url.description: With type exchange: the endpoint the runtime fetches the server's credential from

Language.description: Its primary language, its own or its definition's; null: none

agentId.description: The agent it was forked from

token.description: The agent's scoped credential for /clients routes
The fork's scoped credential for /clients routes; absent for an OAuth access token's caller, which may not hold one

atMessage.description: Where the fork's history ends. A history index: that message, and the tool results that answer it. A request id: the whole turn that request ran. Default: the last turn that ended, never one still running or waiting on input (409 FORK_POINT_RUNNING for a message in such a turn)

ttlSeconds.description: The fork's lifetime: 60 to 31622400 seconds, or null to live until deleted. Default: until deleted with a key, 86400 without

context.description: Context for the fork's tool servers' identity tokens, instead of the source's (fixed once it is made, as at a create)

systemPromptAppend.description: The fork's own text after the system prompt (e.g. its conversation's context), instead of the source's; "" removes it

modelHeaders.description: The fork's own headers on each model call (e.g. its conversation for attribution), instead of the source's; null removes them

cursor.description: Send as Last-Event-ID on the next poll

queuedRuns.description: Runs accepted and waiting behind it (prompts, steered messages not yet read, continues, executions, resumes)

resume.description: For an agent no node holds, whose unfinished work's loads are put off: how many times, and until when

index.description: The message's index in the agent's history

entries.description: Messages, oldest first; whole turns unless a size bound splits them

next.description: Pass as before for the older page; null at the start of the history

total.description: Messages in the history, the running turn's included

split.description: The page starts inside a turn because of a size bound

token.description: Send as Authorization: Bearer <token>, never in a URL

url.description: Where the browser reaches the runtime

ttlSeconds.description: How long it lives: 5 to 3600 seconds, default 900. Nothing revokes it sooner

scopes.description: What it reads of the agent: GET /v1/agents/{id}/<scope>. Default events, state, history and inputs. children: it reads the same of the agent's background sub-agents (spawn_agent's), by their ids

events.description: Only these event types (message_update, tool_execution_end, ...) reach it; default every one but the runtime's own (codemode, compaction_usage, spend_limit_reached, turn_limit_reached). Outcomes (response) and snapshots always do, an outcome only as whether and why its run stopped

redact.description: Fields it does not see: usage.cost, a response's provider cost, in messages, snapshots and history

subject.description: Whom it is for, in your app (a user id)

cancelled.description: The ids of the queued runs the stop cancelled

queued.description: cancel (default): the runs queued behind the running one (prompts, steered messages not yet read, continues, executions) are cancelled too, each ending with code cancelled, so nothing runs after the stop. keep: only the running turn is stopped, and the next queued run starts

children.description: abort (default): the agent's running background sub-agents (spawn_agent) are aborted too, and their notifications follow with status aborted. keep: they go on

reset.description: false: the agent has no context yet (it never ran), and nothing was written

keptMessages.description: History messages the new context kept after the summary

entries.description: Journal entries in the context's range

bytes.description: Their serialized bytes, as AGENT_CONTEXT_RANGE_MAX_BYTES counts them

before.description: The context's range before the reset

summary.description: What the agent is told of its earlier conversation, as a compaction summary. Default: that the operator reset it on this date because it was too large to load, and that its full history remains in its history and files

keepMessages.description: How many of the latest history messages the new context keeps after the summary (0 to 20, default 0). It never starts on a tool result whose call it does not keep

path.description: Where the agent sees the file: attach it as {path}

maxOutputTokens.description: Replaces the most its model writes in one response; null removes it (the model's maximum)

temperature.description: Replaces its model's sampling temperature; null removes it (the provider's default). Refused (400) when the agent's model or thinking level, after this change, takes none

dataCollection.description: Replaces its OpenRouter calls' data policy; null removes it (OpenRouter's default)

language.description: Replaces its primary language from its next turn; null removes it. Set here on an agent from a definition, it stays when the definition is applied

keyScope.description: The key scope its model calls take keys from first; null for the tenant's keys. Applying a definition keeps it

spendLimit.description: A new budget from now, applied at once, ahead of queued runs; null removes it

bucket.description: The bucket of its subject's credit its runs spend from, applied at once; null: "default"
